name: Centro and the Costanera
tagline: The riverfront, the market and the sea lions
description: Valdivia's centre along the Rio Calle-Calle, with the Feria Fluvial market on the water where sea lions haul out to wait for offcuts, the shops, the restaurants and the bus terminal. It is compact and walkable, and the riverfront promenade is the city's main public space.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the market, the river and the restaurants on foot
pros: The riverside market and its sea lions
All shops, services and the terminal walkable
Boats down the river leave from the quay
cons: The highest rents in the city
Rain, for most of the year

name: Isla Teja
tagline: The university island across the bridge
description: The island across the Pedro de Valdivia bridge holding the Universidad Austral campus, the botanical garden, the historical museum in a German settler mansion and the Kunstmann brewery road beyond. It is green, quiet and academic, five minutes on foot from the centre.
bestFor: Anyone connected to the university, and those wanting green quiet close in
pros: University campus and botanical garden on the island
Five minutes across the bridge to the centre
Quieter and greener than the centre
cons: Student housing dominates the rental market

name: Barrios Bajos
tagline: The riverside neighbourhood downstream, local and cheaper
description: A residential district along the river downstream of the centre, historically working-class and with a strong neighbourhood identity, now holding some of the better value housing in the city. The river path runs through it and the centre is a fifteen-minute walk upstream.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a real neighbourhood at a lower rent
pros: River path and a genuine local community
Fifteen minutes on foot to the centre
cons: Some flood exposure along the river

name: Niebla and Corral (18 km west)
tagline: The Spanish forts at the river mouth
description: The coastal settlements where the river meets the Pacific, with seventeenth-century Spanish fortifications on both banks that once made this the most heavily defended harbour on the Pacific coast. A ferry crosses between them. It is windswept, wooded and quite different in feel from the city.
bestFor: Stays wanting the coast and the forts rather than the city
pros: The Spanish forts and the river mouth
Pacific coast and forest immediately there
Ferry between the two banks is part of daily life
cons: Windier and wetter than the city

name: Punucapa and the Wetlands
description: The area north of the city along the Rio Cruces, where the 1960 earthquake sank the land and created the Carlos Anwandter wetland sanctuary, home to black-necked swans and reachable by kayak or boat. Punucapa village sits among apple orchards and cider makers on the far bank.
bestFor: Stays organised around kayaking and the wetlands
pros: The nature sanctuary and its birdlife by kayak
cons: Twenty-five minutes from the city, partly by water
Wet, which is the whole point of the wetland
